issues.legal_issue: A court ordering a tenant’s eviction on a landlord’s application must consider compensation required by the governing eviction rule.
material_facts: The High Court ordered the tenant’s eviction on the landlord’s application under a provision whose proviso required consideration of compensation.
The High Court did not consider that proviso.
The parties agreed that the tenant should receive compensation equivalent to two years’ rent, and the Supreme Court modified the judgment accordingly.
issues.conclusion: Consideration of the compensation proviso was mandatory. The Supreme Court modified the judgment to award the compensation agreed by the parties.
issues.legal_principle: The proviso to Section 21(1) of the U.P. Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972 had to be considered when ordering eviction on an application under Section 21(1)(a). No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.landlord_eviction_proceeding: A landlord applied to have a tenant evicted.
predicates.eviction_order_made: A court ordered the tenant’s eviction on the landlord’s application.
predicates.governing_rule_requires_tenant_compensat: The rule governing the eviction requires compensation for the tenant in the circumstances.

issues.definition: When a landlord’s eviction proceeding results in an eviction order and the governing rule requires tenant compensation, the court must consider that compensation.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant may be given time to leave premises subject to an undertaking to deliver possession and not transfer possession to another person.
material_facts: The tenant and landlord agreed that the tenant could remain in the premises temporarily before handing over possession.
The Supreme Court conditioned that arrangement on the tenant undertaking to hand over vacant and peaceful possession and not to induct another person or otherwise part with possession.
The Court provided that failure to give the undertaking or breach of its conditions would end the protection allowing the tenant to remain.
issues.conclusion: The tenant was allowed to remain temporarily, subject to giving the required undertaking and complying with its conditions; otherwise, the order granting time to vacate would cease to apply.
issues.legal_principle: The Court made a conditional order in accordance with the parties’ agreement, requiring an undertaking to hand over possession and not to induct another person or otherwise part with possession. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this arrangement.

predicates.eviction_order_under_review: A court’s eviction order is before a higher court for review.
predicates.parties_agree_to_temporary_extension: The tenant and landlord agree that the tenant may remain temporarily before leaving the premises.
predicates.tenant_undertakes_to_deliver_possession_: The tenant undertakes to deliver possession and not to induct another person or otherwise transfer possession.

issues.definition: When an eviction order is under review, the parties agree to a temporary extension, and the tenant gives the specified undertaking, the tenant may remain temporarily subject to that undertaking.
